title: Linear function forms
ced_evidence: 2.2.A.1 "f(x) = b + mx"; 2.2.A.2 "f(x) = yi + m(x − xi) based on a known slope, m, and a point, (xi, yi)"

title: Two distinct values determine these sequences and functions
body: Arithmetic sequences, linear functions, geometric sequences, and exponential functions can each be determined by two distinct sequence or function values.
ced_evidence: 2.2.B.3 "can be determined by two distinct sequence or function values"

title: General form of an exponential function
ced_evidence: 2.3.A.1 "f(x) = ab^x, with the initial value a, where a ≠ 0, and the base b, where b > 0, and b ≠ 1"

title: Shape and extrema of exponential functions
body: A general-form exponential function is always increasing or always decreasing, its graph is always concave up or always concave down, and it has no extrema except on a closed interval and no points of inflection.
ced_evidence: 2.3.A.3 "always increasing or always decreasing, and their graphs are always concave up or always concave down"

title: Building an exponential model from two input-output pairs
body: \begin{cases} ab^{x_1}=y_1 \\ ab^{x_2}=y_2 \end{cases}\quad\text{solve the system for } a \text{ and } b \text{ in } f(x)=ab^{x}
ced_evidence: 2.5.A.3 "The initial value and the base can be found by solving a system of equations resulting from the two input-output pairs."

title: Natural base e
body: The natural base e, approximately 2.718, is often used as the base in exponential functions that model contextual scenarios.
ced_evidence: 2.5.A.6 "The natural base e, which is approximately 2.718"

title: Residual plot
body: A residual plot graphs the residuals of a regression (actual dependent value minus the value predicted by the model) on the vertical axis against the independent variable on the horizontal axis, and a model is justified as appropriate if the plot appears without pattern.
ced_evidence: 2.6.B.1 "a residual of a regression is the actual value of the dependent variable value minus the value predicted by the function regression model"

title: Composition is not commutative
body: Composition of functions is not commutative: f∘g and g∘f are typically different functions, so f(g(x)) and g(f(x)) are typically different values.
ced_evidence: 2.7.A.3 "The composition of functions is not commutative"

title: Building and decomposing compositions
body: How the CED has students construct a composition and rewrite a function as a composition.

items.label: Analytic construction
items.meaning: Substitute g(x) for every instance of x in f to get f(g(x)).

items.label: Numerical or graphical construction
items.meaning: Calculate or estimate values for (x, f(g(x))).

items.label: Decomposition
items.meaning: Break an analytic function into less complicated functions, where the variable in one function replaces each instance of the function it was composed with.

items.label: Additive transformation
items.meaning: Vertical and horizontal translations are the composition of g(x) = x + k with f.

items.label: Multiplicative transformation
items.meaning: Vertical and horizontal dilations are the composition of g(x) = kx with f.

ced_evidence: 2.7.B.2 "substituting g(x) for every instance of x in f"; 2.7.C.2 and 2.7.C.3 "composition of g(x) = x + k with f" / "g(x) = kx with f"

title: Contextual restrictions on inverses
body: Besides restricting a function's domain to make it invertible, contextual restrictions may also limit the applicability of an inverse function.
ced_evidence: 2.8.B.5 "contextual restrictions may also limit the applicability of an inverse function"

title: Logarithmic scale
body: On a logarithmic scale, each unit represents a multiplicative change of the base of the logarithm (for base 10, the units might be 10^0, 10^1, 10^2, ...).
ced_evidence: 2.9.A.3 "On a logarithmic scale, each unit represents a multiplicative change of the base of the logarithm"

title: Graph and ordered pairs of log vs. exponential
body: For b>0 and b≠1, the graph of f(x)=log_b x is the reflection of the graph of g(x)=b^x over h(x)=x, so if (s,t) is on g then (t,s) is on f.
ced_evidence: 2.10.A.4 "a reflection of the graph of the exponential function"; 2.10.A.5 "then (t, s) is an ordered pair of the logarithmic function"

title: Recognizing logarithmic behavior via additive transformation
body: If g(x)=f(x+k) with k≠0 for a general-form logarithmic f, its input values are not proportional over equal-length output intervals; but if the input values of g(x)=f(x+k) for any function f are proportional over equal-length output intervals, then f is logarithmic.
ced_evidence: 2.11.A.3 "if the input values of the additive transformation function, g(x) = f(x + k), of any function f are proportional over equal-length output value intervals, then f is logarithmic"
